structures.name: ICA cervical right

provenance.confidence: Reference-guided; depth and calibre estimated

structures.description: The cervical ICA extends from the common carotid bifurcation to the external opening of the carotid canal. It ascends in the carotid space with the internal jugular vein and vagus nerve and normally gives no branches in the neck.

structures.name: ICA petrous right

provenance.confidence: Reference-guided; depth and calibre estimated

structures.description: In the NYU classification, the petrous ICA extends from entry into the carotid canal to the petrolingual ligament. Its vertical and horizontal portions pass through the petrous temporal bone and over the cartilage of the foramen lacerum. It is accompanied by sympathetic fibres derived from the superior cervical ganglion and by a venous plexus.

structures.name: ICA cavernous right

provenance.confidence: Reference-guided; depth and calibre estimated

structures.description:
From the petrolingual ligament to the proximal dural ring.

Course: the vessel runs superiorly along the [posterior clinoid process](#structure-landmark.ica.posterior-clinoid.right) to the [anterior clinoid process](#structure-landmark.ica.anterior-clinoid.right) before passing through the dural ring. Within the cavernous sinus it lies superomedially to the abducens nerve, and medial to CN III, CN IV, and the ophthalmic and maxillary divisions of CN V and the trigeminal (Gasserian) ganglion.

The NYU classification includes the clinoid and dural-ring transition within the paraophthalmic segment. The regional ring boundary is estimated here; the atlas does not resolve a separate dural-ring surface.

structures.name: ICA paraophthalmic right

provenance.confidence: Reference-guided; depth and calibre estimated

structures.description: In the NYU classification, the paraophthalmic ICA extends from the estimated proximal dural ring to the posterior communicating artery origin. It includes the clinoid and ophthalmic regions and therefore spans the transition from extradural to intradural ICA. The ophthalmic origin alone does not reliably identify the distal dural ring.

structures.name: ICA posterior communicating right

provenance.confidence: Reference-guided; depth and calibre estimated

structures.description: From the [PCOM](#structure-artery.anterior.posterior_communicating_right) ostium to the [anterior choroidal artery](#structure-artery.anterior.anterior_choroidal_right) ostium.

provenance.confidence: Reference-guided; depth and calibre estimated

structures.description: In the NYU classification, the anterior choroidal ICA segment is the short arterial region bearing the anterior choroidal artery origin. It lies between the posterior communicating segment and the terminal ICA.

structures.name: ICA terminus right

provenance.confidence: Reference-guided; depth and calibre estimated

structures.description:

This segment contains a variable number of perforating arteries to the anterior perforating substance, which contribute to the collateral reconstitution in Moyamoya disease. Anastomoses are found with the posterior choroidal arteries and ACA.

structures.name: ACA right
aliases: ACA A1 A2 A3 A4 A5 right

provenance.confidence: Reference-guided; depth and calibre estimated

structures.description:
The ACA is the medial terminal division of the [ICA](#structure-artery.anterior.internal_carotid_right), originating lateral to the optic chiasm and beneath the anterior perforated substance.

ACA territory includes the medial frontal and parietal lobes, extending variably over the convexity, in equilibrium with MCA branches.

structures.name: ACA A2 right

provenance.confidence: Reference-guided; depth and calibre estimated

structures.description: The A2 segment is the postcommunicating ACA between the anterior communicating artery region and the rostrum-genu region of the corpus callosum. It ascends in the interhemispheric fissure and gives variable orbitofrontal, frontopolar and perforating branches.

structures.name: ACA A3 right

provenance.confidence: Reference-guided; depth and calibre estimated

structures.description: The A3 segment of the ACA curves around the genu of the corpus callosum in the pericallosal cistern. It continues into the supracallosal distal ACA; callosomarginal and cortical branch origins vary.

structures.name: ACA A4 right

provenance.confidence: Reference-guided; depth and calibre estimated

structures.description: The A4 segment is the supracallosal ACA over the anterior body of the corpus callosum, posterior to the A3 curve around the genu and anterior to the conventional A5 boundary near the coronal plane. It gives callosal and medial hemispheric branches.

structures.name: ACA A5 right

provenance.confidence: Reference-guided; depth and calibre estimated

structures.description: The A5 segment is the posterior supracallosal continuation of the ACA beyond the conventional coronal-plane boundary. It supplies callosal and medial parietal territories and may communicate with posterior pericallosal PCA branches.

structures.name: Vertebral V1 right

provenance.confidence: Reference-guided; tissue depth and calibre estimated

structures.description: The preforaminal V1 segment extends from the vertebral origin to its first transverse foramen. Entry is most often at C6; C4, C5, C7 and other entry variants occur. An aortic arch origin, especially on the left, is associated with variable entry levels and does not determine a single C4 entry. The atlas does not resolve individual cervical transverse foramina.

structures.name: Vertebral V2 right

provenance.confidence: Reference-guided; tissue depth and calibre estimated

structures.description: The V2 segment of the vertebral artery ascends through successive cervical transverse foramina from its first entry, usually at C6, to the transverse foramen of C2. It is accompanied by sympathetic fibres and the vertebral venous plexus.

structures.name: Vertebral V3 right

provenance.confidence: Reference-guided; tissue depth and calibre estimated

structures.description: Starts at the foramen transversarium of the axis (C2). The artery turns laterally and ascends, passing through the transverse foramen of the atlas (C1). It then curves medially and is directed towards the [foramen magnum](#structure-landmark.foramen-magnum.midline). It imprints a [groove on the posterior arch of the atlas](#structure-landmark.atlas-groove.right), which may rarely form a bony ring called the [arcuate foramen](#structure-landmark.arcuate-foramen.right) (a possible risk factor for paediatric ischaemic stroke).

structures.name: Vertebral V4 right

provenance.confidence: Reference-guided; tissue depth and calibre estimated

structures.description: The intradural V4 segment begins where the vertebral artery penetrates the dura near the craniocervical junction and [foramen magnum](#structure-landmark.foramen-magnum.midline). Passage through the posterior atlanto-occipital membrane belongs to the preceding extradural course and is distinct from dural penetration. V4 ascends anteromedially along the medulla and joins its counterpart to form the [basilar artery](#structure-artery.posterior.basilar), usually near the pontomedullary junction. The precise dural entry is not separately segmented in this atlas.

structures.name: Confluence of sinuses

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The confluence joins the [superior sagittal](#structure-vein.superior_sagittal), [straight](#structure-vein.straight), and [occipital sinuses](#structure-vein.occipital_sinus) and drains into the transverse sinuses.

structures.name: Superior sagittal sinus

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The superior sagittal sinus runs in the attached superior margin of the falx cerebri towards the confluence of sinuses. It receives superficial cerebral bridging veins and meningeal and diploic tributaries. The vein of Trolard may provide a major lateral hemispheric connection, but individual venous dominance varies.

structures.name: Straight sinus

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The straight sinus is an unpaired structure located at the junction between the falx and tentorium in the midline, and it follows a straight course posteriorly. It receives blood from the [inferior sagittal sinus](#structure-vein.inferior_sagittal), [vein of Galen](#structure-vein.galen), posterior cerebral veins, superior cerebellar veins, and falx cerebri, and drains into the [confluence of sinuses](#structure-vein.confluence).

structures.name: Inferior sagittal sinus

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: This lies in the inferior edge of the falx parallel to the [superior sagittal sinus](#structure-vein.superior_sagittal). It receives blood from the anterior corpus callosum, cingulate gyrus, medial cerebral hemispheres, and the falx. It joins the [vein of Galen](#structure-vein.galen) to form the [straight sinus](#structure-vein.straight).

structures.name: Occipital sinus

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The occipital sinus usually drains superiorly to the [confluence](#structure-vein.confluence) but may drain inferiorly to the sigmoid or [marginal sinuses](#structure-vein.marginal). It is often hypoplastic or absent in adults.

structures.name: Marginal sinus

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The marginal sinus encircles the foramen magnum and is connected to a network of adjacent venous structures including the [clival plexus](#structure-vein.basilar_plexus) anteriorly, the vertebral venous plexus inferiorly, and sigmoid sinuses laterally.

structures.name: Vein of Galen

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The great cerebral vein of Galen is a short deep venous trunk beneath the splenium of the corpus callosum. It receives the internal cerebral veins and variable basal and posterior fossa tributaries, then joins the inferior sagittal venous system at the anterior end of the straight sinus.

structures.name: Internal jugular vein right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: Together with the vertebral venous plexus, the IJV is the largest drainage pathway for the brain, face, and neck. It is the continuation of the [sigmoid sinus](#structure-vein.sigmoid.right) in the jugular foramen, runs vertically in the carotid sheath in the neck, and joins the subclavian vein to form the brachiocephalic vein. Its tributaries include the [inferior petrosal sinus](#structure-vein.inferior_petrosal.right), anterior condylar vein, facial vein, lingual vein, pharyngeal vein, superior thyroid vein, and middle thyroid vein.

structures.name: Sigmoid sinus right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: This is the anteromedial inferior continuation of the [transverse sinus](#structure-vein.transverse.right) and ends within the jugular fossa. It receives blood from the pons and medulla. It also connects to the scalp veins through the mastoid and condylar veins.

structures.name: Transverse sinus right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The transverse sinuses arise at the [confluence of sinuses](#structure-vein.confluence) and sweep around anterolaterally, confined by the tentorium. They receive veins from the temporal and occipital lobes, particularly the [vein of Labbé](#structure-vein.labbe.right), cerebellar veins, and the [superior petrosal sinus](#structure-vein.superior_petrosal.right). Hypoplasia of one or the other is common, usually the left.

structures.name: Cavernous sinus right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The cavernous sinuses are located on each side of the pituitary fossa. They are an important bidirectional confluence of the intracranial and extracranial venous systems. The sinus contains the ICA, its sympathetic plexus, and the abducens nerve (CN VI). Within the lateral wall, from superior to inferior, are CN III, CN IV, CN V1, and CN V2. The cavernous sinuses connect to the ophthalmic veins, [pterygoid plexus](#structure-vein.pterygoid_plexus.right), [superior petrosal sinus](#structure-vein.superior_petrosal.right), [inferior petrosal sinus](#structure-vein.inferior_petrosal.right), [basilar plexus](#structure-vein.basilar_plexus), and contralateral cavernous sinus through the intercavernous sinuses.

structures.name: Superior petrosal sinus right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description:
These run in the petrosal ridge to connect the posterior aspect of the [cavernous sinus](#structure-vein.cavernous.right) to the junction of the [transverse](#structure-vein.transverse.right) and [sigmoid sinuses](#structure-vein.sigmoid.right). They may receive blood from supra- or infratentorial structures.

The superior petrosal venous complex receives cerebellar and brainstem tributaries. Its anterior and posterior sinus segments, including communication with the [cavernous sinus](#structure-vein.cavernous.right), vary; a single obligatory cavernous outflow pattern is not implied.

structures.name: Inferior petrosal sinus right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The inferior petrosal sinus runs along the petro-occipital junction from the cavernous sinus towards the jugular bulb or upper internal jugular vein. Its jugular termination and connections with clival and infratentorial veins vary.

structures.name: Sphenoparietal sinus right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: This dural channel follows the lesser sphenoid wing and drains into the [cavernous sinus](#structure-vein.cavernous.right). It communicates with adjacent meningeal and diploic channels. Its relationship to the superficial Sylvian veins is variable and terminology differs between references. The represented [superficial middle cerebral vein](#structure-vein.superficial_middle_cerebral.right) enters the cavernous region separately.

structures.name: Superficial middle cerebral vein right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The superficial middle cerebral (Sylvian) vein arises in the Sylvian fissure and drains the adjacent operculum. It empties anteriorly into the [cavernous sinus](#structure-vein.cavernous.right) or [pterygoid venous plexus](#structure-vein.pterygoid_plexus.right). In this selected drainage pattern it enters the cavernous region independently of the dural lesser-sphenoid-wing channel.

structures.name: Superior anastomotic vein of Trolard right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The vein of Trolard is a variable superior anastomotic superficial cerebral vein connecting the superficial Sylvian venous system with the superior sagittal sinus. It drains adjacent frontoparietal cortex and may be small, duplicated or absent.

structures.name: Posterior anastomotic vein of Labbé right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The vein of Labbé is a variable inferior anastomotic superficial cerebral vein connecting temporal or superficial Sylvian drainage with the transverse sinus region. Its size, number and insertion vary, and it may be the dominant temporal venous outlet.

structures.name: Frontal cortical vein right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: Frontal cortical veins drain the frontal surface through a variable superficial venous network. Superior and medial channels commonly reach the superior sagittal sinus, while inferior frontal channels may join superficial Sylvian or basal drainage.

structures.name: Parietal cortical vein right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: Parietal cortical veins drain the parietal surface into variable superficial collectors. Superior channels commonly reach the superior sagittal sinus, while lateral channels may communicate with the Sylvian and anastomotic venous systems.

structures.name: Internal cerebral vein right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The paired internal cerebral veins form near the foramen of Monro, commonly through the union of the anterior septal and superior thalamostriate veins, with variable choroidal tributaries and venous-angle arrangements. They drain subependymal and choroidal territories and pass posteriorly in the velum interpositum along the roof of the third ventricle. The two internal cerebral veins unite beneath the splenium to contribute to the [great cerebral vein](#structure-vein.galen). The basal veins may join the internal cerebral or great cerebral veins, or follow other recognised drainage variants. The atlas shows a selected bilateral drainage pattern.

structures.name: Basal vein of Rosenthal right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The basal vein of Rosenthal is a deep venous collector beginning near the anterior perforated substance, commonly receiving anterior cerebral, deep middle cerebral and inferior striate drainage. It courses around the midbrain and usually reaches the Galenic system. Its segments may be incomplete and alternative petrosal, tentorial or other drainage routes occur.

structures.name: Superior thalamostriate vein right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The thalamostriate vein primarily drains the lateral subependymal, posterior frontal, and anterior parietal veins, as well as the caudate nucleus and internal capsule. It receives minimal drainage from the thalamus itself, but does receive the superior choroidal vein. It runs along the thalamocaudate groove towards the [internal cerebral vein](#structure-vein.internal_cerebral.right).

structures.name: Anterior septal vein right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The anterior septal vein starts in the frontal horn of the lateral ventricle, formed from the deep medullary veins of the anterior frontal lobe. It runs posteriorly to join the [thalamostriate vein](#structure-vein.thalamostriate.right) at the venous angle near the foramen of Monro. It may instead join the internal cerebral vein more posteriorly.

structures.name: Superior choroidal vein right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.name: Deep middle cerebral vein right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The deep middle cerebral vein is formed from insular and inferior striate veins. It joins the [anterior cerebral vein](#structure-vein.anterior_cerebral.right) to form the [basal vein of Rosenthal](#structure-vein.basal.right).

structures.name: Superior petrosal vein right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The superior petrosal vein is a major collector of the petrosal cerebellar surface and adjacent brainstem. One or several trunks enter the superior petrosal sinus, receiving variable cerebellopontine fissure, peduncular and pontine tributaries.

structures.name: Lateral mesencephalic vein right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The lateral mesencephalic veins connect the [basal vein of Rosenthal](#structure-vein.basal.right) to lateral brainstem and medullary fissure veins. They act as a crucial collateral drainage route, especially when the basal vein is discontinuous, draining posteriorly to infratentorial veins.

structures.name: Vein of the cerebellopontine fissure right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: Anterior hemispheric veins draining the petrosal surface converge near the flocculus to form the vein of the cerebellopontine fissure, which drains into the [superior petrosal sinus](#structure-vein.superior_petrosal.right) through the [superior petrosal vein](#structure-vein.superior_petrosal_vein.right).

structures.name: Inferior vermian vein right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The paired inferior vermian veins lie in the cerebellovermian fissure and drain the inferior vermis and medial suboccipital surface into the [torcular](#structure-vein.confluence) or transverse sinus, directly or via a tentorial sinus.

structures.name: Inferior hemispheric vein right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: Inferior hemispheric veins can run longitudinally or transversely. Longitudinal veins join superior hemispheric veins and drain into a dural or tentorial sinus, while transverse veins are associated with cerebellar fissures and drain into the [inferior vermian vein](#structure-vein.inferior_vermian.right).

structures.name: External jugular vein right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The external jugular vein usually forms from the posterior division of the retromandibular vein and the posterior auricular vein. It descends superficially across sternocleidomastoid and usually drains into the subclavian vein. Its formation and tributaries vary.

structures.name: Retromandibular vein right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The maxillary vein converges with the [superficial temporal vein](#structure-vein.superficial_temporal.right) to form the retromandibular vein. It contributes to drainage of the deep face and scalp into the [external jugular vein](#structure-vein.external_jugular.right).

structures.name: Maxillary vein right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The [pterygoid plexus](#structure-vein.pterygoid_plexus.right) becomes the maxillary vein, which later converges with the [superficial temporal vein](#structure-vein.superficial_temporal.right) to form the [retromandibular vein](#structure-vein.retromandibular.right).

structures.name: Pterygoid venous plexus right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The pterygoid venous plexus occupies the infratemporal region around the pterygoid muscles, with superficial and deep components. It drains predominantly through the maxillary vein and communicates with the facial vein, orbital veins and cavernous sinus through variable channels.

structures.name: Superficial temporal vein right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The superficial temporal vein drains the scalp and converges with the [maxillary vein](#structure-vein.maxillary.right) to form the [retromandibular vein](#structure-vein.retromandibular.right).

structures.name: Posterior auricular vein right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The posterior auricular vein contributes to drainage of the scalp and posterolateral neck into the [external jugular vein](#structure-vein.external_jugular.right).

structures.name: Facial vein right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The facial vein begins near the medial canthus as the continuation of angular venous drainage and descends across the face. It commonly joins the anterior retromandibular division to form the common facial vein draining to the internal jugular vein. It communicates with the ophthalmic veins and pterygoid plexus; venous patterns vary.

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.name: Deep facial vein right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative
provenance.revision145: Local native-foramen fit; topology and connections retained. See docs/foramina-revision145.md.

structures.name: Superior ophthalmic vein right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The superior ophthalmic vein begins in the anterior superomedial orbit and runs posteriorly towards the superior orbital fissure to drain into the cavernous sinus. It communicates with facial and other orbital veins. This atlas includes an inferior ophthalmic tributary joining it in the posterior orbit.

structures.name: Inferior ophthalmic vein right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The inferior ophthalmic vein drains posteriorly into the [superior ophthalmic vein](#structure-vein.superior_ophthalmic.right), which continues to the [cavernous sinus](#structure-vein.cavernous.right). A communicating limb is retained towards the [pterygoid venous plexus](#structure-vein.pterygoid_plexus.right) through the inferior orbital fissure. This is a selected teaching pattern; orbital venous anatomy is variable.

structures.name: Emissary vein of foramen ovale right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The emissary vein of the foramen ovale is a variable communication between the cavernous sinus region and the pterygoid venous plexus through the foramen ovale. Its calibre and haemodynamic direction vary.

structures.name: Vertebral vein right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The vertebral venous system receives the [suboccipital plexus](#structure-vein.suboccipital_plexus.right) and condylar communications. It accompanies the vertebral artery in the transverse foraminal canal, with an upper plexiform arrangement that commonly lies ventrolateral to the artery and a larger lower collecting vein. The vein leaves the lower transverse foramina and drains to the brachiocephalic vein. This atlas displays a representative dominant channel and a suboccipital plexus; the cervical vertebrae and complete intraforaminal plexus are not modelled.

structures.name: Suboccipital venous plexus right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The suboccipital venous plexus contributes to the vertebral venous system through the [vertebral artery venous plexus](#structure-vein.vertebral.right) and [deep cervical vein](#structure-vein.deep_cervical.right). It also communicates with condylar veins.

structures.name: Deep cervical vein right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The deep cervical vein receives tributaries of the [suboccipital venous plexus](#structure-vein.suboccipital_plexus.right). It follows the deep cervical artery to end in the IJV or brachiocephalic vein.

structures.name: Anterior condylar vein right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The anterior condylar vein, or vein of the hypoglossal canal, connects the [marginal sinus](#structure-vein.marginal) and adjacent skull-base venous network to the [internal jugular vein](#structure-vein.internal_jugular.right) at the bulb. The anterior condylar confluence is formed by the anterior and lateral condylar veins and tributaries of the clival plexus.

structures.name: Lateral condylar vein right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The lateral condylar vein connects the jugular and anterior condylar region with the [suboccipital plexus](#structure-vein.suboccipital_plexus.right) and vertebral venous system.

structures.name: Internal jugular vein left

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: Together with the vertebral venous plexus, the IJV is the largest drainage pathway for the brain, face, and neck. It is the continuation of the [sigmoid sinus](#structure-vein.sigmoid.left) in the jugular foramen, runs vertically in the carotid sheath in the neck, and joins the subclavian vein to form the brachiocephalic vein. Its tributaries include the [inferior petrosal sinus](#structure-vein.inferior_petrosal.left), anterior condylar vein, facial vein, lingual vein, pharyngeal vein, superior thyroid vein, and middle thyroid vein.

structures.name: Sigmoid sinus left

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: This is the anteromedial inferior continuation of the [transverse sinus](#structure-vein.transverse.left) and ends within the jugular fossa. It receives blood from the pons and medulla. It also connects to the scalp veins through the mastoid and condylar veins.

structures.name: Transverse sinus left

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The transverse sinuses arise at the [confluence of sinuses](#structure-vein.confluence) and sweep around anterolaterally, confined by the tentorium. They receive veins from the temporal and occipital lobes, particularly the [vein of Labbé](#structure-vein.labbe.left), cerebellar veins, and the [superior petrosal sinus](#structure-vein.superior_petrosal.left). Hypoplasia of one or the other is common, usually the left.

structures.name: Cavernous sinus left

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The cavernous sinuses are located on each side of the pituitary fossa. They are an important bidirectional confluence of the intracranial and extracranial venous systems. The sinus contains the ICA, its sympathetic plexus, and the abducens nerve (CN VI). Within the lateral wall, from superior to inferior, are CN III, CN IV, CN V1, and CN V2. The cavernous sinuses connect to the ophthalmic veins, [pterygoid plexus](#structure-vein.pterygoid_plexus.left), [superior petrosal sinus](#structure-vein.superior_petrosal.left), [inferior petrosal sinus](#structure-vein.inferior_petrosal.left), [basilar plexus](#structure-vein.basilar_plexus), and contralateral cavernous sinus through the intercavernous sinuses.

structures.name: Superior petrosal sinus left

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description:
These run in the petrosal ridge to connect the posterior aspect of the [cavernous sinus](#structure-vein.cavernous.left) to the junction of the [transverse](#structure-vein.transverse.left) and [sigmoid sinuses](#structure-vein.sigmoid.left). They may receive blood from supra- or infratentorial structures.

The superior petrosal venous complex receives cerebellar and brainstem tributaries. Its anterior and posterior sinus segments, including communication with the [cavernous sinus](#structure-vein.cavernous.left), vary; a single obligatory cavernous outflow pattern is not implied.

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.name: Superior ophthalmic vein left

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The superior ophthalmic vein begins in the anterior superomedial orbit and runs posteriorly towards the superior orbital fissure to drain into the cavernous sinus. It communicates with facial and other orbital veins. This atlas includes an inferior ophthalmic tributary joining it in the posterior orbit.

structures.name: Inferior ophthalmic vein left

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The inferior ophthalmic vein drains posteriorly into the [superior ophthalmic vein](#structure-vein.superior_ophthalmic.left), which continues to the [cavernous sinus](#structure-vein.cavernous.left). A communicating limb is retained towards the [pterygoid venous plexus](#structure-vein.pterygoid_plexus.left) through the inferior orbital fissure. This is a selected teaching pattern; orbital venous anatomy is variable.

structures.name: Emissary vein of foramen ovale left

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The emissary vein of the foramen ovale is a variable communication between the cavernous sinus region and the pterygoid venous plexus through the foramen ovale. Its calibre and haemodynamic direction vary.

structures.name: Vertebral vein left

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The vertebral venous system receives the [suboccipital plexus](#structure-vein.suboccipital_plexus.left) and condylar communications. It accompanies the vertebral artery in the transverse foraminal canal, with an upper plexiform arrangement that commonly lies ventrolateral to the artery and a larger lower collecting vein. The vein leaves the lower transverse foramina and drains to the brachiocephalic vein. This atlas displays a representative dominant channel and a suboccipital plexus; the cervical vertebrae and complete intraforaminal plexus are not modelled.

structures.name: Suboccipital venous plexus left

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The suboccipital venous plexus contributes to the vertebral venous system through the [vertebral artery venous plexus](#structure-vein.vertebral.left) and [deep cervical vein](#structure-vein.deep_cervical.left). It also communicates with condylar veins.

structures.name: Deep cervical vein left

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The deep cervical vein receives tributaries of the [suboccipital venous plexus](#structure-vein.suboccipital_plexus.left). It follows the deep cervical artery to end in the IJV or brachiocephalic vein.

structures.name: Anterior condylar vein left

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The anterior condylar vein, or vein of the hypoglossal canal, connects the [marginal sinus](#structure-vein.marginal) and adjacent skull-base venous network to the [internal jugular vein](#structure-vein.internal_jugular.left) at the bulb. The anterior condylar confluence is formed by the anterior and lateral condylar veins and tributaries of the clival plexus.

structures.name: Lateral condylar vein left

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The lateral condylar vein connects the jugular and anterior condylar region with the [suboccipital plexus](#structure-vein.suboccipital_plexus.left) and vertebral venous system.

structures.name: Anterior intercavernous sinus

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The anterior intercavernous sinus connects the cavernous sinuses across the anterior aspect of the pituitary gland. Its size and continuity vary.

structures.name: Posterior intercavernous sinus

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The posterior intercavernous sinus connects the cavernous sinuses behind the pituitary gland. Its size and continuity vary, and it may communicate with adjacent sellar or clival channels.

structures.name: Basilar venous plexus

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The basilar or clival plexus connects with the cavernous sinuses posteriorly and with the [marginal sinus](#structure-vein.marginal) and anterior condylar venous network below. It forms a variable plexiform network along the posterior clivus, with communications to both [inferior petrosal sinuses](#structure-vein.inferior_petrosal.right). The displayed interconnected channels represent one selected reference pattern.

structures.name: Anterior communicating vein

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The anterior cerebral veins are connected by the anterior communicating vein in half the population. This contributes to the anterior venous circle in the suprasellar cistern.

structures.name: Posterior communicating vein

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The posterior communicating vein is a transverse venous communication in the interpeduncular region linking the basal venous systems. Together with adjacent hypothalamic and mesencephalic channels, it may contribute to a posterior venous circle; its development and calibre vary.

structures.name: Precentral cerebellar vein

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The precentral cerebellar vein, an unpaired vein, ascends in the quadrigeminal cistern behind the tectal plate to drain into the [vein of Galen](#structure-vein.galen). It can merge with the [superior vermian vein](#structure-vein.superior_vermian) to form the superior cerebellar vein or drain directly into the vein of Galen independently.

structures.name: Superior vermian vein

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The superior vermian veins drain the superior vermis and the medial parts of the superior cerebellar hemispheres. The anterior veins drain into the [vein of Galen](#structure-vein.galen), and the posterior veins drain into the [confluence of sinuses](#structure-vein.confluence).

structures.name: Median anterior pontomesencephalic vein

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The midline brainstem veins form a continuous anastomotic venous channel comprising the median anterior pontomesencephalic, median anterior pontine, and median anterior medullary veins. Blood may flow cranially to the posterior communicating vein or peduncular veins, or caudally into the spinal veins.

structures.name: Median anterior pontine vein

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The median anterior pontine vein forms part of the continuous midline anastomotic channel between the [median anterior pontomesencephalic vein](#structure-vein.anterior_pontomesencephalic) and [median anterior medullary vein](#structure-vein.anterior_medullary). It runs on the anterior surface of the pons, near the midline, normally between the basilar artery and brainstem.

structures.name: Median anterior medullary vein

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The median anterior medullary vein continues inferiorly as the [anterior spinal vein](#structure-vein.anterior_spinal). It forms part of the continuous midline venous channel on the anterior brainstem.

structures.name: Anterior spinal vein

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: The anterior spinal vein is the inferior continuation of the [median anterior medullary vein](#structure-vein.anterior_medullary). Blood may flow cranially through the brainstem venous channel or caudally into the spinal veins.

structures.name: Transverse pontine vein right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: A transverse pontine vein crosses the anterior pontine surface and communicates with longitudinal and lateral pontine venous channels. At the midline it normally passes between the basilar artery and the pons.

structures.name: Vein of the pontomedullary sulcus right

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.name: Transverse pontine vein left

provenance.confidence: Note-guided connections and angiogram-guided morphology fitted to retained bone; calibre and depth remain illustrative

structures.description: A transverse pontine vein crosses the anterior pontine surface and communicates with longitudinal and lateral pontine venous channels. At the midline it normally passes between the basilar artery and the pons.

provenance.confidence: Skull-registered atlas context; not patient-specific

structures.description: The pons is the brainstem segment between the midbrain and medulla. Its ventral surface faces the prepontine cistern and basilar artery, while its dorsal surface contributes to the floor of the fourth ventricle. Atlas boundaries are approximate.

structures.name: Pons, left

provenance.confidence: Skull-registered atlas context; not patient-specific

structures.description: The fourth ventricle is the CSF space between the dorsal pons and upper medulla anteriorly and the cerebellar roof structures posteriorly. structures.name: Medulla oblongata, left

provenance.confidence: Skull-registered atlas context; not patient-specific

structures.description: The medulla is the caudal brainstem between the pons and spinal cord. Its ventral surface bears the pyramids and olives; its upper dorsal surface contributes to the floor of the fourth ventricle. Atlas boundaries are approximate.

structures.name: Medulla oblongata, right

provenance.confidence: Skull-registered atlas context; not patient-specific

structures.description: The medulla is the caudal brainstem between the pons and spinal cord. Its ventral surface bears the pyramids and olives; its upper dorsal surface contributes to the floor of the fourth ventricle. Atlas boundaries are approximate.

structures.name: Tentorium cerebelli, right

provenance.confidence: Skull-registered atlas context; not patient-specific

structures.description: The tentorium cerebelli is a dural fold separating the occipital cerebral hemispheres from the cerebellum. Its free medial edge bounds the tentorial incisura; its junction with the falx contains the straight sinus. Atlas boundaries are approximate.

structures.name: Falx cerebri

provenance.confidence: Skull-registered atlas context; not patient-specific

structures.description: The falx cerebri is the midline dural fold between the cerebral hemispheres. The superior sagittal sinus lies in its attached superior margin, the inferior sagittal sinus in its free inferior margin, and the straight sinus along its junction with the tentorium. Atlas boundaries are approximate.

structures.name: Lateral ventricle, right

provenance.confidence: Skull-registered atlas context; not patient-specific

structures.description: The lateral ventricle is a C-shaped CSF cavity within a cerebral hemisphere, with frontal, temporal and occipital horns around a central body and atrium. It communicates with the third ventricle through the interventricular foramen. Atlas boundaries are approximate.

structures.name: Lateral ventricle, left

provenance.confidence: Skull-registered atlas context; not patient-specific

structures.name: Thalamus, right

provenance.confidence: Skull-registered atlas context; not patient-specific

structures.name: Third ventricle

provenance.confidence: Skull-registered atlas context; not patient-specific

structures.description: The third ventricle is a midline CSF cavity between the thalami and hypothalamic regions. It communicates with the lateral ventricles through the interventricular foramina and with the fourth ventricle through the cerebral aqueduct. Atlas boundaries are approximate.

structures.name: Midbrain, right

provenance.confidence: Skull-registered atlas context; not patient-specific

structures.description: The midbrain lies between the diencephalon and pons. Its ventral surface contains the cerebral peduncles and interpeduncular region, while the colliculi form its dorsal tectum around the cerebral aqueduct. Atlas boundaries are approximate.

structures.description: The caudate nucleus curves alongside the lateral ventricle, with its head beside the frontal horn, body along the ventricular body and tail following the temporal horn. Atlas boundaries are approximate.

structures.name: Fornix, right

provenance.confidence: Skull-registered atlas context; not patient-specific

structures.description:
One of the paired dural venous channels accompanying the [middle meningeal artery](#structure-artery.eca.maxillary.mma.right.left).

Here “anterior” identifies its position beside the frontal MMA route, rather than a separate arterial division. The represented receiving connection is the [lesser-wing (sphenoparietal) sinus](#structure-vein.sphenoparietal.left). The short basal and cranial endings are capped in this reconstruction; a complete route to the pterygoid plexus or superior sagittal sinus is not modelled. Exact bony canal containment remains unverified.

structures.name: PICA p2 lateral medullary right

provenance.confidence: Reference-guided; tissue depth and calibre estimated

structures.description: The lateral medullary segment courses beside the medulla, from the inferior olive region to the lower cranial nerve rootlet plane. Its passage in relation to cranial nerves IX, X and XI varies between individuals. These rootlets are not separately modelled, so the distal boundary is a regional anatomical estimate.

structures.name: PICA p3 tonsillomedullary right

provenance.confidence: Reference-guided; tissue depth and calibre estimated

structures.description: The tonsillomedullary segment begins behind the lower cranial nerves. It descends towards the inferior pole of the cerebellar tonsil, forms the caudal loop, then ascends along the medial tonsillar region to its midpoint. This atlas shows a representative loop fitted to the registered tonsil; loop height varies in normal anatomy.

structures.name: PICA p4 telovelotonsillar right

provenance.confidence: Reference-guided; tissue depth and calibre estimated

structures.description: The telovelotonsillar segment continues from the ascending medial tonsillar midpoint through the upper cerebellomedullary fissure. Its cranial loop relates to the superior tonsillar pole below the tela choroidea and inferior medullary velum, before the vessel leaves the fissures for the cerebellar surface. Choroidal branches supply the fourth ventricular plexus. The tela, velum and fourth ventricular plexus are not separately segmented here.

structures.name: PICA p5 cortical right

provenance.confidence: Reference-guided; tissue depth and calibre estimated

structures.description: The cortical segment begins where the PICA leaves the fissures around the tonsil, vermis and hemisphere.
